newsitem.title: USA: Blast at U.S. nuclear site caused chaos: LA Times.
newsitem.headline: Blast at U.S. nuclear site caused chaos: LA Times.

text.p: The response to a chemical explosion at the Hanford Nuclear Reservation in May was flawed to the point of failure, exposing workers to danger and not notifying outside authorities for hours, the Los Angeles Times reported in Saturday's editions.

"In a series of extraordinary admissions, the Department of Energy and Fluor Daniel Hanford, inc., manager of the huge nuclear site in central Washington State detailed a series of failures in almost every link of the emergency response chain...," the newspaper reported from Seattle.
The incident took place at Hanford's Plutonium Reclamation Facility.

The Department of Energy admitted the chemicals were not stored properly. It said workers "were ordered outside a trailer to walk through a toxic plume, had to drive themselves to the hospital four hours after the event and did not have their radiological tests scrutinized until a month after the accident," the Times said.

The report "paints a picture of a late-night chemical explosion followed by hours of apparent chaos in which workers were given conflicting orders; procedures for emergency response were nonexistent or ignored and there was no early notification to civilian authorities...," the newspaper reported.
"The findings of this report are not good. In fact, they're downright ugly," Lloyd Piper, the Energy Department's acting manager at the plant told the Times.
"We failed in some key areas of responsibility. Our actions in the wake of the explosion did not meet our high exxpectations," Piper told the newspaper.
